newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's Emaar reported planning residential complex.
newsitem.headline: UAE's Emaar reported planning residential complex.

text.p: New Dubai-based firm Emaar Properties plans to build a 100-unit residential complex in Dubai which it will sell to United Arab Emirates and other Gulf Arabs, newspapers reported on Tuesday.

The reports also said a six-member board of directors, made up of businessmen including Minister of State for Financial and Industrial Affairs Mohammad Khalfan bin Kharbash, was elected during the company's first general assembly meeting on Monday. A chairman had not yet been chosen.

"The residential complex will be built on a 50 million dirham ($13.6 million) plot donated by Dubai's Crown Prince and UAE's Minister of Defence Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum," Al-Khaleej daily said. Company officials put building costs at about 55 million dirhams.
Al-Khaleej said Dubai was in the final stages of reviewing a UAE law that would allow sale of residential units to other Gulf Arabs who are currently restricted to owning only land.
The project is the second to be announced by Emaar which has a capital of one billion dirhams. In May it said it would build a 170 million dirham high-rise commercial centre.
